title: The Turnaround
coreMove: Rank inherited assets by recovery value, then cut even proud pieces when they weaken the company that must survive.
sourcePressure: Bill Anders and General Dynamics show outsider discipline inside a damaged enterprise where portfolio triage and rational downsizing matter more than preserving inherited scale.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Do not write a generic crisis chapter; every scene must show triage among inherited commitments, with contraction serving recovery rather than image.

sourceAnchors.name: Bill Anders
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar pairs Chapter 3 with Bill Anders and General Dynamics and says he reset the company through portfolio triage and rational downsizing.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Bill Anders walks into the lesson as a reminder that recovery sometimes starts by deciding what the company must stop being.

sourceAnchors.name: General Dynamics
sourceAnchors.detail: The sidecar says William A. Anders served as vice chairman and CEO of General Dynamics from 1990 to 1994 after roles in government, General Electric, and Textron.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: General Dynamics gives the triage problem its weight because inherited scale had to be judged rather than admired.

counterintuition: Saving morale means saving every unit
examples: proud product line from legacy draft
robotics team with too many builds

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: No more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'.
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: At least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human.
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: ship-repair yard deciding which dock contracts survive after a debt covenant breach
exampleSpecs.audience: a yard president with three legacy service lines and one profitable repair niche
exampleSpecs.stakes: missing the covenant again will put the yard under bank control
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Thomas lays each contract folder under a red, yellow, or green tag and cancels the prestige naval refit bid because it consumes dry-dock days the profitable emergency repair work needs.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: rainwater pooled in a dry-dock inspection groove

exampleSpecs.domain: rural clinic network closing one satellite service to save urgent-care coverage
exampleSpecs.audience: a medical director facing three thinly staffed locations
exampleSpecs.stakes: keeping every service open would leave urgent care unsafe by August
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sophie moves colored pins on the staffing map and closes the low-volume dermatology day so nurses can cover urgent care where patients actually arrive.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: colored map pins scattered across a county clinic map

exampleSpecs.domain: independent games studio after a failed launch
exampleSpecs.audience: a studio founder attached to three prototype expansions
exampleSpecs.stakes: nine weeks of payroll left and one salvageable core game loop
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took Lukas one payroll forecast to freeze two admired expansions and assign every remaining developer to the single loop with evidence of player retention.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a bug board with three colored columns and one column crossed out

exampleSpecs.domain: city arts festival recovering after a sponsor collapse
exampleSpecs.audience: a festival director deciding which venues to keep
exampleSpecs.stakes: trying to preserve the full map would cancel the festival entirely
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: What is the smallest festival still worth holding? Aanya cuts the admired waterfront stage first because security costs would drain the whole recovery budget.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a folded festival map with a blue waterfront circle

exampleSpecs.domain: regional freight carrier after losing its largest retail account
exampleSpecs.audience: a fleet manager protecting routes that once signaled market reach
exampleSpecs.stakes: empty miles are burning fuel cash needed for core medical deliveries
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: James asks dispatch to name which routes still pay for their trucks, then parks the longest prestige route and reallocates drivers to contracted medical deliveries.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a diesel receipt curled on top of a route profitability report

exampleSpecs.domain: language school with too many course levels after enrollment drops
exampleSpecs.audience: a director worried parents will read cancellations as failure
exampleSpecs.stakes: keeping every level alive leaves each class too small to teach well
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Marit cross out the least viable intermediate sections, merge students into fewer stronger rooms, and explain that recovery means protecting learning quality rather than preserving the old catalog.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a course catalog with sticky notes covering half the schedule
mustAvoid: classroom generic; make it a language-school operating decision

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference

skillTargets: rank inherited commitments by recovery value
separate rational downsizing from toughness theater
spot when preserving scale weakens the core
choose a contraction that improves future strength rather than optics

tryThisNowSpec: Draw three boxes labeled protect, sell or stop, and undecided for one overloaded system; place one inherited commitment in each box using recovery value only.
